title: Case management for frequent emergency department attenders and 12-month death or intensive care admission
subtitle: Matched case-control evaluation of a regional case management program
statement: A case management program for adults with eight or more ED visits in 12 months has run at the tertiary ED since March 2023 and at two community EDs since 2024. Visit counts fall after a peak regardless of the program, so the health authority needs an evaluation on outcomes that matter: death or intensive care admission within 12 months. Because these outcomes are rare and exposure must be read from case management files, a matched case-control design is proposed.
whoAffected: Adults who frequently attend the region's EDs, many with chronic illness, mental health needs, addiction or housing instability; their families; ED staff and case managers; and the health authority deciding on funding.
whatHurts: Frequent attenders die or are admitted to intensive care at high rates, and a program judged on visit counts could be kept or stopped for the wrong reasons.
currentPractice: Case managers build care plans for enrolled patients; the program is monitored by visit counts only.
whyNow: The health authority's funding review, and approvals and data-sharing already in place at all three sites.
constraints: Two research assistants for about 15 hours a week each until June 2027; file reading must fit that time. No contact with patients or families. Data leave each site only as de-identified extracts under the regional data-sharing agreement. The health authority expects a report by September 2027.
patientCenteredGoal: People who frequently need the ED are kept alive and out of intensive care by support that reaches them early.
summary: Problem framed as a matched case-control evaluation of case management on death or ICU admission.
